parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
• Draw a line AB 4 cm from the edge of the ray-trace sheet and in the middle of the paper,
as shown in Fig. 1.1.
• Draw a line CD parallel to line AB and 10 cm from it.
• Draw a normal to line AB at a point N in the centre of line AB. Point N must be an equal
distance from the top and bottom of the sheet.
• Extend the normal to line CD and label the point at which it crosses line CD with the
letter L.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Draw a line EF, through point N, as shown in Fig. 1.1 and at an angle θ = 5°.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
• Place the plane mirror on line EF with the reflecting surface facing to the right.
• Place the screen with a slit on line CD and arrange the lamp so a ray of light shines
along line LN.
• Mark the ray that is reflected from the mirror, using a small cross at a suitable distance
from point N. Label this cross G.
• Remove the mirror, screen and lamp from the ray-trace sheet.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
• Draw a line joining point N and point G. Extend this line until it meets line CD.
• Label the point at which line NG meets line CD with the letter H.
• Measure, and record in Table 1.1, the length a of line LH.

parts.text:

parts.text:
The thermometer must remain in the clamp throughout the experiment.
• Use the measuring cylinder to pour 100 cm of hot water into beaker A.
• Place the thermometer in the water in beaker A.
• In the first row of Table 2.1, record the temperature θ of the water at time t = 0 and
immediately start the stopclock.
• Record, in Table 2.1, the temperature θ of the water at times t = 30 s, 60 s, 90 s, 120 s,
150 s and 180 s.
• Remove the thermometer from the beaker.
